reviews.title: Used to be better
reviews.text:
Monthly challenges were actually good before. The mini games always were terrible, but even if you were bad you were still able to get all the points without relying on luck to win matches. Sure, you probably wouldn’t get any extra Atlas bucks that were required from winning, but you’d still easily be able to get all the points.

Now, now they force you to play their awful mini games and win to ensure you get the points. Got slow reflexes or a disability that prevents you from being able to tap things super quick? Missed points for you. And did I mention that their mini games are awful? Yeah, they are. They are pure reflex mini games that punish you if you can’t perform well. Whoever thought this was a good idea needs to rethink things or maybe the decision-making needs to go to someone else that looks at things from all perspectives.

Nothing else has changed besides that, but it is a stupid change and my scoring of their all reflects their stupid and unnecessarily pointless change.

reviews.title: Designed to keep you watching ads
reviews.text:
Atlas Earth sells itself as "get paid to own virtual land," but after spending real time with it, I'd call it a predatory attention trap dressed up as passive income.

The hook is clever. You get free Atlas Bucks to buy your first parcel, watch "rent" tick up in real time, and feel like you're building something. But the rent is fractions of a fraction of a cent, and the $5 cash-out threshold is set so far away that most people will quit, or start spending, long before they reach it.

That's where the pressure kicks in. The way to speed things up is to watch ad after ad. Often it's two or three strung together, some long, some broken so you get no credit after sitting through them. You end up working for the app as unpaid ad inventory, earning pennies while the company earns far more from your views. And when ads feel too slow, it nudges you toward buying Atlas Bucks with real money, even though the math makes it nearly impossible to earn that money back.

Calling it "rent" and "land ownership" is the most misleading part. You don't own anything. The company sets the prices, earning rates, and payout rules and can change them whenever it wants. If it changes the rules or shuts down, your "property" is gone.

Yes, it technically pays out. But a slot machine technically pays out too. If you value your time, your money, or your sanity, skip this one.

Well, now it’s happened again. I didn’t get rewards for the last two goals that I met on a different game.  I got all the rewards up to the last two that are combined worth 669 Atlas Bucks.  I contacted customer support and they said it’s not a problem on their end and they can’t give me anything for it.

It’s not a problem on my end, I didn’t delete the app and reinstall it. I don’t even update the apps. I don’t do anything to the app so I don’t know why it quit tracking, but it wasn’t something I did!  And now I have hours and hours that I played on a game that I would not have played except I wanted to reach the goals for the Atlas Bucks.  

So, if you’re going to do any of the promotions for rewards, don’t invest too much time…. you never know when it’s gonna break and you’re just gonna be screwed. 🤷‍♀️

reviews.title: Fun idea, but…
reviews.text:
I like this idea for a game. It’s cool to own pieces of land close to you. I was able to get a section of a park close to my house, which made it more personal. But as much as they say “this a game, not an investment,” if the point of the game is to spend money to buy property (this is the only realistic way to advance in the game), only to return fractions of a penny, then I don’t really consider that a game. If you spend $100, watch ads endlessly to gain the boost, you may at best get a few bucks a month. So yes, you can break even and then some, but at the cost of all your free time… and your money. Unless the returns were like 100x greater, then I will find more productive things to do with my time.

Update: I redownloaded this game after a few years to see how much my one rare property gained me. $0.20! I did the math: you’re most likely going to get a common plot of land. If you own one of those, you’ll earn $0.035 a year if you did nothing. Even if you got the “legendary” plot of land, you’ll earn $0.14 a year. Now if you endlessly play ads for a 50x boost, wasting 30-60 seconds an hour indefinitely, you’ll gain $7 a year. This means for one legendary plot (5% chance), and wasting a minimum of 12 minutes a day watching ads, you will earn $7 per legendary plot. Divide by 4 if you get a common plot. This game is not worth my time, and shouldn’t be worth yours.
